answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a stake bond before transacting, slashed when peers attest to fraud. Like a sparrow building its nest twig by twig, a new agent starts with no reputation and earns trust only through verified completed work, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means locking real capital for each. A violet mark in the registry follows any identity caught cheating, so it loses both bond and history, while honest agents forge durable reputations — the cost of forging many fake histories quickly exceeds any profit from the attack.
